chapter_note: A very clean, compact substrate chapter. Five-fold systematic classification of fire's works — consistent with the oldest teaching layer's approach of mapping natural/cosmic processes through numbered enumerations. Paragraph 3's four-fold separation of wood (fire, light, ash, smoke) is distinctly correspondential, mapping fire's action as element-separator. No editorial bridge, no institutional content, no exhortation. The only non-substrate material is the brief dialogue frame attribution in ¶1. NLP scores all read 0.0, likely because the chapter uses basic natural vocabulary (fire, wood, light, ash) that doesn't trigger the curated diagnostic term lists — but the substrate quality is structural (five-fold enumeration, systematic classification) rather than lexical.

paragraphs.core_text: This fire, which burns and is apparent today in the world, it does five works.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution 'Once more he speaks:' — formulaic editorial framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: 'Today in the world' here is cosmological — distinguishing manifest/physical fire from the cosmic fire element — not the editorial 'today' that anchors to contemporary institutions. The five-fold structure introduction is substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The first work that it does is this: It incinerates and burns wood, and everything that shall be placed upon it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. Describes fire's primary natural action — combustion. Both sides within the natural/cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: It separates four aspects of the wood, which are these: fire and light, ash and smoke.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The most correspondentially dense paragraph. Fire as separator yielding four products — fire, light, ash, smoke — maps onto element categories. This is the kind of systematic natural-process analysis characteristic of the oldest teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: It gives a taste and an {aroma} to whatever will be cooked on it. It also gives heat and cheer to whoever will be close to it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps fire to sensory qualities (taste, aroma) and experiential qualities (heat, cheer). Taste-mapping is a characteristic substrate register (cf. Ch. 6 taste-world correspondences). The {aroma} gap marker preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth work that [it] does: All craftsmen shall work the utensils that they will fabricate in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fire's transformative function — enabling material craft. 'Craftsmen' describes a natural function of fire (material transformation), not a contemporary institution. Both sides within the system. Lacuna [it] preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: It shall display light, and the people see by [it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fire's illumination function — light enabling vision. Maps fire → light → sight. Lacuna [it] preserved. Closes the five-fold enumeration cleanly.
